title: Cost-Aware Feature Gate (CAG) PRD
author: Priya Rao
summary: Product requirements and rollout plan for a Cost-Aware Feature Gate (CAG) that lets customers enable or disable optional fidelity features dynamically based on token spend, latency budget, and subscription entitlements.
body:
Overview

This document defines the Cost-Aware Feature Gate (CAG): a server-side and client-facing mechanism to control opt-in fidelity features (e.g., higher-quality quantization, expanded context, optional reranking, RTT-expensive tools) by associating them with explicit cost and SLO constraints. The CAG lets Redwood reduce surprise bill impact for customers, improve predictability of cluster economics, and provide a gradual commercial path for fidelity add-ons.

Goals

- Provide a single, auditable control plane for enabling/disabling fidelity features per-tenant, per-route, and per-session based on cost signals.
- Reduce outbound charge variability by preventing accidental activation of expensive fidelity features.
- Make fidelity toggles composable with existing rollout and canary tooling (A/B, percent rollouts, time-windowed experiments).
- Surface actionable telemetry and billing hooks so customers can see projected spend before a gate opens.

Non-goals

- CAG will not replace full contract negotiation or manual enterprise pricing tiers; it is additive to billing contracts.
- CAG will not change token metering semantics; it augments which generation paths are allowed.

Terminology

- Fidelity Feature: any optional capability that increases per-token or per-request cost (examples: full-context attention, n-best reranker, high-precision float kernels).
- Gate Rule: predicate that decides whether a fidelity feature is allowed for a request.
- Budget Window: sliding or fixed window used to measure spend or token counts (e.g., 24h, 30d).
- Cost Signal: metric used in rules (token spend, latency, request rate, credit balance).

Success metrics (90-day targets)

1. 80% reduction in incidents where customers inadvertently generate >2x expected spend due to fidelity features.
2. 30% of new enterprise customers adopt at least one CAG policy during onboarding.
3. Average time to detect and block expensive feature activation reduced from 3 hours to <10 minutes (alerting + autotoggle).

Scope and Use Cases

Primary use cases:
- Developer sandbox: prevent high-fidelity features for free trial accounts after projected spend > $X/day.
- Tiered customers: allow high-fidelity features only for platinum tenants or when a dedicated capacity route is used.
- Adaptive fallback: automatically disable reranking if average latency for the last 5m exceeds target SLO.
- Pre-flight gating: preview projected extra cost in Console before enabling a feature.

Rules engine primitives

Each Gate Rule is constructed from primitive building blocks:
- MATCH(scope) -> {tenant, route, api_key, session}  // single selector
- CONDITION(metric, comparator, value) -> e.g. (token_spend_30d < 50000)
- ACTION(allow | deny | conditionalBeta)
- OVERRIDES(priority, ttl, approver)

Example rules:
1) Deny: if tenant.account_type == \"trial\" AND token_spend_24h > 1000 -> ACTION(deny)
2) Allow: if tenant.fidelity_entitlement contains \"premium-rerank\" -> ACTION(allow)
3) Conditional: if latency_5m_avg > 250ms -> ACTION(deny) with automatic rollback window 10m

Policy configuration table

| Field | Type | Description | Example |
|-------|------|-------------|---------|
| id | string | unique policy id | cag-policy-2026-09 |
| scope | enum | tenant|route|session | tenant |
| fidelity_feature | string | feature id (see Feature Catalog) | rerank-v2 |
| metric | string | cost or perf signal | token_spend_24h |
| comparator | enum | lt, lte, gt, gte, eq | gt |
| threshold | number | numeric threshold | 1000 |
| action | enum | allow, deny, conditional | deny |
| priority | int | higher wins on conflict | 100 |
| active | bool | enabled state | true |
| created_by | string | owner | se-ops@redwood.com |

API contract (internal control plane)

POST /api/v1/cag/policies
Request (JSON):
{
  \"scope\": \"tenant\",
  \"selector\": { \"tenant_id\": \"acct-123\" },
  \"fidelity_feature\": \"rerank-v2\",
  \"metric\": \"token_spend_24h\",
  \"comparator\": \"gt\",
  \"threshold\": 1000,
  \"action\": \"deny\",
  \"priority\": 100
}

Response: 201 Created with policy id and etag for optimistic concurrency.

Runtime evaluation (pseudocode)

1. Request arrives -> extract scope (tenant, route, session).
2. Gather latest metrics from metering store (token spend, latency) for relevant window.
3. Evaluate applicable policies ordered by priority.
4. If first matching policy.action == deny -> short-circuit and return feature_disabled response header.
5. If conditional -> return feature_allowed=true with telemetry flags indicating degraded mode.

Feature toggle response contract

- HTTP header: X-Redwood-Fidelity:<feature_id>=allowed|denied|conditional
- JSON telemetry: \"fidelity_decisions\": [{\"feature\": \"rerank-v2\", \"decision\": \"denied\", \"policy_id\": \"cag-policy-2026-09\"}]

Console and pre-flight UX

- Console: new CAG tab under Tenant Settings. Shows active policies, projected delta spend per feature, and a simulator for 24h/30d windows.
- Pre-flight preview API: POST /api/v1/cag/simulate with payload (tenant_id, feature_id, projected_requests, avg_tokens_per_request) -> returns projected_cost_delta and list of matching policies.

Telemetry, metrics and billing hooks

Minimum telemetry to capture per request:
- fidelity_flags (list of features requested)
- fidelity_decision (allow|deny|conditional)
- matched_policy_id
- projected_feature_cost (float)
- tokens_consumed

Key dashboards and alerts:
- Policy hits: rate of denies per tenant (alert if > 5% of requests denied for a paying tenant).
- Cost projection delta: sum(projected_feature_cost) per tenant over 24h (alert if > 2x baseline).
- Autotoggle events: count of automatic policy-triggered rollout changes.

Billing integration notes

- Metering service must expose a near-real-time token_spend_24h signal with <= 30s staleness for active tenants.
- For usage-based charging of optional features, billing engine will use fidelity_decision telemetry to label line-items. 
- A reconciliation job will run daily to validate decisions vs billed events and populate disagreements for finance review.

Example Console table (CSV-friendly)

policy_id,scope,feature,metric,threshold,action,active,priority,created_by
cag-2026-09,tenant,rerank-v2,token_spend_24h,1000,deny,true,100,priya.roa@redwood.com

Rollout plan (6 phases)

1. Prototype (2 weeks): server-only implementation with hard-coded policies; internal tenants only.
2. Canary (4 weeks): expose read-only Console view + simulation API for 10 pilot customers. Collect feedback.
3. Read/Write GA (8 weeks): full policy CRUD in Console, RBAC controls, optimistic concurrency.
4. Billing integration (4 weeks): tagging line-items and daily reconciliation. Close coordination with Finance.
5. Enterprise features (6 weeks): policy approvals, SLA exemptions, override workflows with audit trail.
6. Broad Launch (2 weeks): public docs, playbook, migration checklist for customers.

Safety and rollback

- All deny actions default to tenant-level overrides for enterprise contracts with \"waived\" flags.
- Every policy write requires an audit entry; accidental mass-deny can be reverted via \"emergency-unblock\" runbook.
- Circuit breaker: global autotoggle suppression if > 5% tenants experience unexpected denials in a 5m window.

Ownership and stakeholders

- Product lead: Priya Rao (owner).
- Eng: Runtime (policy engine) - owner: Julian Kim.
- Metrics & Billing: owner: Nadia Gomez.
- Security & Compliance: review for audit logging and RBAC - owner: Ethan Brooks.

Open questions and decisions to make

1. How to prioritize conflicting rules from route-level vs tenant-level? (Proposed: priority integer wins).
2. Which features are classified as \"fidelity\" by default? Need a Feature Catalog entry.
3. Should conditional decisions impose soft-fallback costing or simply disable the feature?

Appendices

A. Sample policy YAML (for repo and IaC)
---
- id: cag-tenant-trial-spend-block
  scope: tenant
  selector:
    tenant_id: acct-xyz
  fidelity_feature: rerank-v2
  metric: token_spend_24h
  comparator: gt
  threshold: 1000
  action: deny
  priority: 100
  active: true
  created_by: priyarao@redwood.com
---

B. Alerting runbook (short)
1) Pager: oncall-runtime@redwood.com.
2) Check policy service logs for policy id and recent writes.
3) If mass deny observed, execute emergency-unblock: POST /api/v1/cag/_emergency_unblock with approver and incident id (requires SRE + Product signoff).
4) Open ticket in Incident Review board and notify Finance if billing discrepancies observed.

C. Back-of-envelope cost calculation example
- Rerank-v2 adds 0.012 USD per request above baseline.
- Tenant A average 100k requests/day -> projected delta = 1200 USD/day.
- CAG policy denying rerank when token_spend_24h > 1000 prevents an estimated 80% of this delta in the first 48h of onboarding.
